# WithGuard

`WithGuard` is a component for conditionally rendering UI elements based on guard evaluation. It uses the same guard system as route-level guards, making permission logic reusable throughout your application.

## Import

```tsx
import { WithGuard, pass, hidden } from "@tailor-platform/app-shell";
```

The runnable examples also import `useMemo` and `useState` from `react`, and `Button`, `Checkbox`, `Select`, `Spinner`, `Text`, and the `Guard` type from `@tailor-platform/app-shell`.

The previews use local role, subscription, and permission values captured by their guards. They reuse the surrounding AppShell provider without changing its `contextData` or performing real authentication. In an application, read those values from the guard's `{ context }` argument, as shown under [Creating Guards](#creating-guards). Keep each guards array stable with `useMemo` until its inputs change.

## Basic Usage

Choose **Admin** to reveal the protected content, then switch back to **Viewer** to remove it from the DOM. Without a `fallback`, a hidden guard renders nothing.

<example-preview name="basic-usage"></example-preview>

```tsx
function BasicUsage() {
  const [role, setRole] = useState("Viewer");
  const guards = useMemo<Guard[]>(() => [() => (role === "Admin" ? pass() : hidden())], [role]);

  return (
    <div className="max-w-sm space-y-3">
      <Select
        aria-label="Demo role"
        items={["Viewer", "Admin"]}
        value={role}
        onValueChange={(value) => {
          if (value) setRole(value);
        }}
      />
      <Text.p>Current role: {role}</Text.p>
      <WithGuard guards={guards}>
        <Text.p role="status">Admin settings are available.</Text.p>
      </WithGuard>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Props

_Generated from the type surface — first-party props only._

### WithGuardProps

| Prop        | Type        | Default                  | Description                                                                                                                     |
| ----------- | ----------- | ------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `children`  | `ReactNode` | -                        | Content to render when all guards pass.                                                                                         |
| `fallback?` | `ReactNode` | `null (renders nothing)` | Content to render when any guard returns hidden.                                                                                |
| `guards`    | `Guard[]`   | -                        | Guards to evaluate. All guards must pass for children to render. Uses the same Guard type as route guards for full reusability. |
| `loading?`  | `ReactNode` | `null (renders nothing)` | Content to render while guards are being evaluated (for async guards).                                                          |

## Exports

- `WithGuard` — const
- `WithGuardProps` — type

## Guard Functions

WithGuard uses the same `Guard` type as route guards:

```typescript
type Guard = (ctx: GuardContext) => GuardResult | Promise<GuardResult>;

type GuardResult =
  | { type: "pass" } // Allow rendering
  | { type: "hidden" }; // Hide content (render fallback)
```

**Note:** Unlike route guards, `redirectTo()` is **not supported** in WithGuard. Use `hidden()` with a fallback that handles navigation if needed.

### Creating Guards

```tsx
import { type Guard, pass, hidden } from "@tailor-platform/app-shell";

// Simple guard
const requireAuth: Guard = ({ context }) => {
  return context.currentUser ? pass() : hidden();
};

// Async guard with API call
const hasPermission: Guard = async ({ context }) => {
  const canAccess = await fetch("/api/permissions/admin")
    .then((r) => r.json())
    .then((data) => data.allowed);

  return canAccess ? pass() : hidden();
};

// Parameterized guard (curried function)
const isOwner =
  (resourceId: string): Guard =>
  ({ context }) => {
    return context.currentUser?.id === resourceId ? pass() : hidden();
  };
```

## Examples

### Simple Role Check

The [Basic Usage](#basic-usage) example demonstrates role-based visibility without a fallback.

### With Fallback

Show alternative content when a guard fails. Toggle **Premium subscription** to switch between the upgrade prompt and the protected analytics content.

<example-preview name="with-fallback"></example-preview>

```tsx
function WithFallback() {
  const [premium, setPremium] = useState(false);
  const guards = useMemo<Guard[]>(() => [() => (premium ? pass() : hidden())], [premium]);

  return (
    <div className="space-y-3">
      <Checkbox label="Premium subscription" checked={premium} onCheckedChange={setPremium} />
      <WithGuard
        guards={guards}
        fallback={<Text.p role="status">Upgrade to view analytics.</Text.p>}
      >
        <Text.p role="status">Premium analytics are available.</Text.p>
      </WithGuard>
    </div>
  );
}
```

### With Loading State

The local permission check waits briefly so its spinner and loading announcement can be observed without an API. Toggle **Allow permission check** to try both outcomes, or use **Check permission again** to repeat the current check. Each request gets a stable guards array; a new request reevaluates it without changing AppShell's context.

<example-preview name="with-loading-state"></example-preview>

```tsx
function WithLoadingState() {
  const [request, setRequest] = useState({ allowed: false });
  const guards = useMemo<Guard[]>(
    () => [
      async () => {
        await new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, 700));
        return request.allowed ? pass() : hidden();
      },
    ],
    [request],
  );

  return (
    <div className="space-y-3">
      <Checkbox
        label="Allow permission check"
        checked={request.allowed}
        onCheckedChange={(allowed) => setRequest({ allowed })}
      />
      <Button variant="outline" onClick={() => setRequest((current) => ({ ...current }))}>
        Check permission again
      </Button>
      <WithGuard
        guards={guards}
        loading={
          <div role="status" className="flex items-center gap-2">
            <Spinner />
            <Text.span>Checking permission…</Text.span>
          </div>
        }
        fallback={<Text.p role="status">Permission denied.</Text.p>}
      >
        <Text.p role="status">Permission granted.</Text.p>
      </WithGuard>
    </div>
  );
}
```

### Multiple Guards

All guards must pass for content to render. Enable **Admin access** and **Beta feature enabled** in either order; the protected feature appears only when both are enabled.

<example-preview name="multiple-guards"></example-preview>

```tsx
function MultipleGuards() {
  const [admin, setAdmin] = useState(false);
  const [betaEnabled, setBetaEnabled] = useState(false);
  const guards = useMemo<Guard[]>(
    () => [() => (admin ? pass() : hidden()), () => (betaEnabled ? pass() : hidden())],
    [admin, betaEnabled],
  );

  return (
    <div className="space-y-3">
      <Checkbox label="Admin access" checked={admin} onCheckedChange={setAdmin} />
      <Checkbox
        label="Beta feature enabled"
        checked={betaEnabled}
        onCheckedChange={setBetaEnabled}
      />
      <WithGuard
        guards={guards}
        fallback={
          <Text.p role="status">Both admin access and the beta feature are required.</Text.p>
        }
      >
        <Text.p role="status">Beta admin feature is available.</Text.p>
      </WithGuard>
    </div>
  );
}
```

### Parameterized Guards

Use curried functions to create reusable parameterized guards. This preview signs in no one: **alex** is a local fixture for the current user. Change the record's owner to see the ownership check pass or fail. A real ownership guard reads the current user's ID from `{ context }`.

<example-preview name="parameterized-guards"></example-preview>

```tsx
function ParameterizedGuards() {
  const currentUserId = "alex";
  const [ownerId, setOwnerId] = useState("alex");
  const guards = useMemo<Guard[]>(() => {
    const isOwner =
      (resourceOwnerId: string): Guard =>
      () =>
        resourceOwnerId === currentUserId ? pass() : hidden();
    return [isOwner(ownerId)];
  }, [currentUserId, ownerId]);

  return (
    <div className="max-w-sm space-y-3">
      <Text.p>Signed in as: {currentUserId}</Text.p>
      <Select
        aria-label="Record owner"
        items={["alex", "sam"]}
        value={ownerId}
        onValueChange={(value) => {
          if (value) setOwnerId(value);
        }}
      />
      <WithGuard
        guards={guards}
        fallback={<Text.p role="status">Only the record owner can edit.</Text.p>}
      >
        <Text.p role="status">You can edit this record.</Text.p>
      </WithGuard>
    </div>
  );
}
```

### In Sidebar Navigation

Conditionally show navigation items:

```tsx
import { DefaultSidebar, SidebarItem, WithGuard } from "@tailor-platform/app-shell";

const isAdmin = ({ context }) => (context.currentUser?.role === "admin" ? pass() : hidden());

<DefaultSidebar>
  <SidebarItem to="/dashboard" />
  <SidebarItem to="/products" />

  <WithGuard guards={[isAdmin]}>
    <SidebarItem to="/admin" />
    <SidebarItem to="/settings" />
  </WithGuard>
</DefaultSidebar>;
```

### Feature Flags

The [Multiple Guards](#multiple-guards) example combines a feature flag with a role check. Use the same `pass()` / `hidden()` decision when reading a feature flag from `context`.

### Subscription Tiers

The [With Fallback](#with-fallback) example switches between a free-tier prompt and premium content. The fallback can also be a card or an upgrade link owned by your application.

### Dynamic Permissions

The [With Loading State](#with-loading-state) example demonstrates pending, allowed, and denied states with a local delayed check. Replace that check with your permission API in an application; the loading and fallback behavior is unchanged. See [Creating Guards](#creating-guards) for an API-backed guard shape.

### Combining with Route Guards

Reuse the same guards for routes and UI:

```tsx
// guards.ts
export const requireAuth: Guard = ({ context }) => {
  return context.currentUser ? pass() : hidden();
};

export const isAdmin: Guard = ({ context }) => {
  return context.currentUser?.role === "admin" ? pass() : hidden();
};

// routes.tsx
const adminModule = defineModule({
  path: "admin",
  component: AdminPage,
  guards: [requireAuth, isAdmin], // Route-level
});

// component.tsx
<WithGuard guards={[requireAuth, isAdmin]}>
  {" "}
  {/* UI-level */}
  <AdminSettings />
</WithGuard>;
```

## Guard Evaluation

Guards are evaluated in order and stop at the first non-pass result:

```tsx
const guards = [guardA, guardB, guardC];

// If guardA returns hidden(), guardB and guardC are NOT evaluated
<WithGuard guards={guards}>
  <Content />
</WithGuard>;
```

## Performance

### Caching

WithGuard caches guard results while both the `contextData` reference and the `guards` array remain unchanged:

- Guards re-evaluate when either `contextData` or the `guards` array reference changes.
- Other prop changes do not re-evaluate guards.
- Define fixed guards outside the component, or memoize a guards array with the values its functions capture. Creating a new array on an unrelated render starts another evaluation, including another asynchronous check.

### Suspense Integration

Async guards use React Suspense:

- Shows `loading` prop while evaluating
- Renders `children` or `fallback` when complete
- Automatically suspends during evaluation

## Context Data

Guards receive the same context as route guards:

```typescript
// Define context type
declare module "@tailor-platform/app-shell" {
  interface AppShellRegister {
    contextData: {
      currentUser: User | null;
      featureFlags: FeatureFlags;
      permissions: string[];
    };
  }
}

// Use in guards
const hasPermission =
  (perm: string): Guard =>
  ({ context }) => {
    return context.permissions.includes(perm) ? pass() : hidden();
  };
```

## Comparison: WithGuard vs Route Guards

| Feature                     | WithGuard                | Route Guards                |
| --------------------------- | ------------------------ | --------------------------- |
| **Purpose**                 | Conditional UI rendering | Route access control        |
| **Location**                | Inside components        | Module/resource definitions |
| **Supports `pass()`**       | ✅ Yes                   | ✅ Yes                      |
| **Supports `hidden()`**     | ✅ Yes                   | ✅ Yes                      |
| **Supports `redirectTo()`** | ❌ No                    | ✅ Yes                      |
| **Async guards**            | ✅ Yes                   | ✅ Yes                      |
| **Reusable**                | ✅ Yes                   | ✅ Yes                      |

## Best Practices

### Do:

- ✅ Reuse guards between routes and UI
- ✅ Use descriptive guard names (`isAdmin`, `canEdit`)
- ✅ Provide fallback for better UX
- ✅ Show loading state for async guards
- ✅ Cache expensive permission checks

### Don't:

- ❌ Use `redirectTo()` in WithGuard (not supported)
- ❌ Make guards too complex (extract to functions)
- ❌ Forget to handle loading states
- ❌ Skip fallback when hiding important features
- ❌ Duplicate permission logic (reuse guards)

## Accessibility

- Content is fully removed from DOM when hidden (not just visually)
- Screen readers won't announce hidden content
- Loading states should be announced to screen readers
- Fallback content should be accessible

## TypeScript

Full type safety with TypeScript:

```typescript
import { type Guard, type WithGuardProps } from "@tailor-platform/app-shell";

// Type-safe guard
const isAdmin: Guard = ({ context }) => {
  // context is fully typed
  return context.currentUser?.role === "admin" ? pass() : hidden();
};

// Type-safe props
const guardProps: WithGuardProps = {
  guards: [isAdmin],
  children: <AdminPanel />,
  fallback: <AccessDenied />,
};
```

## Troubleshooting

### Guard not re-evaluating

**Problem:** Guard doesn't update when data changes

**Solution:** Ensure `contextData` reference changes:

```tsx
// ❌ Bad - mutating object
context.currentUser.role = "admin";

// ✅ Good - new reference
setContextData({
  ...contextData,
  currentUser: { ...currentUser, role: "admin" },
});
```

### Infinite loading

**Problem:** Loading state never resolves

**Solution:** Ensure async guards return a result:

```tsx
// ❌ Bad - no return
const checkPermission: Guard = async ({ context }) => {
  await fetch("/api/check");
  // Missing return!
};

// ✅ Good - returns result
const checkPermission: Guard = async ({ context }) => {
  const allowed = await fetch("/api/check").then((r) => r.json());
  return allowed ? pass() : hidden();
};
```
